name: Windbrisk Heights
oracle_text:
Hideaway 4 (When this land enters, look at the top four cards of your library, exile one face down, then put the rest on the bottom in a random order.)
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {W}.
{W}, {T}: You may play the exiled card without paying its mana cost if you attacked with three or more creatures this turn.
blocked_sentences: {W}, {T}: You may play the exiled card without paying its mana cost if you attacked with three or more creatures this turn.

needs.what: A per-object, turn-scoped record of having been declared as an attacker this turn, readable from a selector -- e.g. a `selector_keys` entry `attacked_this_turn: true` matched against a set of attacker oids tallied on `TurnLedger` when attackers are declared and cleared with the rest of the ledger at the turn boundary. With it, Windbrisk Heights' unlock is an ordinary intervening condition and needs nothing else new: `{"op": "if", "condition": {"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "attacked_this_turn": true}}, "right": {"const": 3}}, "then": [{"op": "may", "effects": [{"op": "play_exiled"}]}]}`. Note the count must survive the creature leaving the battlefield to be fully correct (an attacker that died in combat still attacked), so the ledger should hold oids rather than be recomputed from live permanents. Wanted identically by the other hideaway lands' siblings that count attackers (Mosswort Bridge counts total power of creatures you control, but Windbrisk Heights, Hellrider-style raid variants and Aggravated Assault/Seize the Day all want the per-object attacker record already requested by relentless_assault).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `attacked_this_turn` in `value_keys` is the closest thing and is per **player**, not per creature: `structs.py:237` stores `attacked: set[int]` of player ids -- its own comment says "a set rather than a count because raid asks only whether it happened" -- and `values.py:273` returns `sum(1 for p in pids if p in ledger.attacked)`, so `{"attacked_this_turn": "you"}` is 1 whether you attacked with one creature or ten. A `cmp` of it against `{"const": 3}` would therefore never be true, and against `{"const": 1}` it would silently turn Windbrisk Heights into a raid land that unlocks off a single attacker -- the approximation this card most invites. The `attacking` selector key is strictly live combat state (`selectors.py:459` answers it with `state.combat and combat.attacking(oid)`, and `end_combat` sets `state.combat = None`), so `{"count": {"attacking": true}}` reads 0 in the postcombat main phase where this ability is most often activated, and it also misses attackers that died during combat. `tapped` catches creatures tapped for mana or by a tapper and misses vigilant attackers. `set_flag`/`has_flag` could record the fact, but only from an ability this card does not print, and the residual gate requires every ability's `text` to be a printed line.
